english: Winter is colder than autumn.
tip: A comparative followed by a bare genitive means than, with no separate word for it: холоднее осени (kholodneye oseni = colder than autumn).

english: They would learn Russian.
tip: бы plus a past-tense verb means would; бы never changes, the verb carries gender and number: бы выучили (by vyuchili = would learn).

english: We should have waited.
tip: следовало бы plus an infinitive means should or ought to: следовало бы подождать (sledovalo by podozhdat = ought to wait).

english: Who would you invite?
tip: кто (kto) becomes кого when it is the object (whom): Кого бы ты пригласил (kogo by ty priglasil = whom would you invite).

english: She would be happy.
tip: In conditionals the past verb still shows gender: была бы (byla by = would be, feminine); a man would say был бы (byl by).

english: Half of the work is already done.
tip: A short passive participle works like is done and agrees with its subject in gender: уже сделана (uzhe sdelana = is already done), feminine.

english: The children ran out of the house.
tip: из plus the genitive means out of and mirrors в (v) plus accusative for going in: из дома (iz doma = out of the house).

english: The restaurant where we had lunch closed.
tip: Use где for where pointing at a place, marking location rather than motion: Ресторан, где (restoran, gde = the restaurant where).

english: The phone that I use is new.
tip: пользоваться (polzovatsya) takes the instrumental, so which appears as которым: телефон, которым я пользуюсь (telefon, kotorym ya polzuyus = the phone I use).

target: Передай мне, пожалуйста, соль и перец.
english: Please pass me the salt and pepper.
tip: The person receiving something goes in the dative: Передай мне (pereday mne = pass me). мне is the dative of я (ya).

target: Комната, в которой стоит пианино, большая.
english: The room in which the piano stands is big.
tip: который (kotoryy) agrees with its noun in gender and number, but its case comes from its own clause: в которой (v kotoroy = in which), feminine, prepositional after в.

target: Что бы ты сделал на моём месте?
english: What would you do in my place?
tip: на моём месте is the set phrase for in my place: на моём месте (na moyom meste = if I were you). месте is prepositional after на.

target: Если бы ты спросил, я бы ответил.
english: If you had asked, I would have answered.
tip: Unreal conditionals put бы in both halves: Если бы ты спросил, я бы ответил (yesli by ty sprosil, ya by otvetil = if you had asked, I would have answered).

target: Этот дом такой же большой, как тот.
english: This house is as big as that one.
tip: As ... as is такой же plus an adjective plus как: такой же большой, как (takoy zhe bolshoy, kak = as big as).

target: Напишите своё имя и фамилию в этом бланке.
english: Write your first and last name on this form.
tip: свой (svoy) means one's own and points back to the subject, replacing мой (moy) or его (yego) when they equal the doer: своё имя (svoyo imya = your own name).

english: My house is closer to school.
tip: ближе pairs with к plus the dative to say closer to: ближе к школе (blizhe k shkole = closer to school).

english: It would be useful to learn a language.
tip: Было бы plus an adjective plus an infinitive makes an impersonal it would be: Было бы полезно (bylo by polezno = it would be useful).

target: Самая холодная зима за десять лет.
english: The coldest winter in ten years.
tip: Superlatives use самый (samyy) before the adjective, both agreeing with the noun: Самая холодная зима (samaya kholodnaya zima = the coldest winter), feminine.

target: Он старше меня на два года.
english: He is two years older than me.
tip: на plus an amount tells you by how much with a comparative: старше на два года (starshe na dva goda = older by two years).

target: Те, кто опоздал, не получат билеты.
english: Those who are late will not get tickets.
tip: кто counts as singular, so its verb stays singular even after plural Те: Те, кто опоздал (te, kto opozdal = those who were late).

target: Вкус домашнего хлеба ни с чем не сравнить.
english: The taste of homemade bread is incomparable.
tip: Russian doubles the negative, ни plus a second negator не: ни с чем не сравнить (ni s chem ne sravnit = cannot be compared to anything).

target: Не трогай эту вазу, она очень старая и хрупкая.
english: Don't touch that vase, it's very old and fragile.
tip: Negative commands normally use the imperfective verb: Не трогай (ne trogay = don't touch), not the perfective тронь (tron).

english: Prices are higher and higher.
tip: всё before a comparative means more and more: всё выше и выше (vsyo vyshe i vyshe = higher and higher).

english: This task is not easier than that one.
tip: та (ta) becomes той in the genitive of comparison: не легче той (ne legche toy = no easier than that one), feminine matching задача (zadacha).

english: Remember this rule!
tip: Запомни (zapomni = remember) is the informal command to one person. For formal or plural, add -те: запомните (zapomnite).

english: Put things here!
tip: сюда (syuda = to here) marks motion toward the speaker. A static location would use здесь (zdes = here) instead.

english: Let's finish work!
tip: Давайте (davayte = let's) plus a perfective we-form makes a suggestion: Давайте закончим (davayte zakonchim = let's finish).

english: Show me the way!
tip: мне (mne = to me) is the dative of я, marking who gets shown something: покажите мне (pokazhite mne = show me).

english: She is the best teacher.
tip: лучшая (luchshaya = best) is the irregular superlative of хороший (khoroshiy = good), not a самый form.

english: The weather is getting warmer.
tip: становится (stanovitsya = becomes) plus a comparative like теплее (teplee = warmer) expresses a gradual change.
